editorial:
Imagine spending a hot summer in Sicily, falling for a beautiful American girl, and then watching her fly away without a second thought. That is exactly what happens to Tanino, a film student who thinks he is way more worldly than he actually is. He is a bit of a dreamer who loves to talk about politics and art, but he has no real experience with the world. When he decides to fly to the U.S. to surprise Sally, he thinks he is in a romantic movie. You will find yourself laughing at his confidence and feeling bad for him as his fantasy starts to fall apart in the face of real American life.

The acting is great because it captures that awkward feeling of being a fish out of water. The pacing is steady, and the funny moments come from how different Tanino's expectations are from the truth. While some parts might feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you want to see this one, I suggest renting it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a movie buff, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality. It is a perfect pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: In the end, Tanino finally realizes that Sally does not love him the way he loves her. He sees that he was just a summer fling to her and that their worlds are too different to ever work. Instead of staying and begging for her love, he accepts the truth. He heads back to Sicily with a new perspective on life, finally growing up and leaving his naive fantasies behind him for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about travel, awkward romance, and growing up.
